decision: Do not promote the rejected v2 candidate or the tested local repairs.

failure_mechanisms.finding: At the first obstacle, an uncertified right-side target opposes the observed left bend. Two contacts leave the car stationary on the road; the no-progress counter labels the endpoint off_track. A one-action road-steering override and late policy handoff do not recover the lap.
A near-center obstacle offset flip is vetoed by both temporal-side and reachability guards. Removing either veto alone leaves the entire action trace and five-contact crash unchanged.

The candidate finishes with four contacts versus zero for control. Raising a global camera clearance floor to two pixels reduces this cell to three contacts but loses a separate candidate-only finish.

The candidate crashes with five contacts; side-hold and high-speed bend guard never alter its applied actions. A global selected-side steering floor rescues this cell but loses ten other candidate finishes in the consumed screen.

camera_clearance_calibration.finding: The same 2.07/1.07-pixel visible side widths preceded both a four-contact pass and a zero-contact pass. Static camera width alone does not predict future vehicle-hull clearance.

limits: All experiments reuse the eight v2 screen geometries and are development evidence only. The frozen v2 confirmation and blind phases remain sealed. No official Linux submission-container certification was available.
